questions.text: What renders after one click?
questions.prompt:
function Counter() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);

  const handleClick = () => {
    setCount(count + 1);
    setCount(count + 1);
    setCount(count + 1);
  };

  return <button onClick={handleClick}>{count}</button>;
}
  • A: 3
  • B: 1
  • C: 0
  • D: 2

questions.text: What's wrong here? The counter shows 1 and then stops forever.
questions.prompt:
function Timer() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);

  useEffect(() => {
    const id = setInterval(() => setCount(count + 1), 1000);
    return () => clearInterval(id);
  }, []);

  return <h1>{count}</h1>;
}
  • A: clearInterval runs too early
  • B: the interval closes over count from the first render
  • C: setCount is not batched inside setInterval
  • D: the empty dep array is illegal here

questions.text: How many re-renders does this cause — in React 17, and in React 18+?
questions.prompt:
function App() {
  const [a, setA] = useState(0);
  const [b, setB] = useState(0);

  const handleClick = () => {
    setTimeout(() => {
      setA(x => x + 1);
      setB(x => x + 1);
    }, 0);
  };

  return <button onClick={handleClick}>{a}{b}</button>;
}
  • A: 1 then 1
  • B: 2 then 1
  • C: 1 then 2
  • D: 2 then 2

questions.text: What's the log order?
questions.prompt:
function Parent() {
  useEffect(() => console.log('parent effect'), []);
  return <Child />;
}

function Child() {
  useEffect(() => console.log('child effect'), []);
  return null;
}
  • A: parent effect, child effect
  • B: child effect, parent effect
  • C: order is not guaranteed
  • D: only parent effect

questions.text: Child is memoized but still logs on every parent render. Why?
questions.prompt:
const Child = React.memo(({ style, onSelect }) => {
  console.log('child render');
  return <div style={style} onClick={onSelect} />;
});

function Parent() {
  const [n, setN] = useState(0);
  return (
    <>
      <button onClick={() => setN(n + 1)}>{n}</button>
      <Child style={{ color: 'red' }} onSelect={() => console.log('pick')} />
    </>
  );
}

questions.prompt:

  const [user, setUser] = useState(null);

    <AuthCtx.Provider value={{ user, setUser }}>

}

questions.text: Switching documents keeps the previous draft in the box. What's the one-character-ish fix?
questions.prompt:
function Editor({ docId }) {
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState('');
  return <textarea value={draft} onChange={e => setDraft(e.target.value)} />;
}

// parent
<Editor docId={selectedId} />
  • A: add useEffect(() => setDraft(''), [docId])
  • B: render <Editor key={docId} docId={selectedId} />
  • C: move draft to the parent
  • D: wrap Editor in React.memo

questions.text: What happens when userId goes from "42" to null?
questions.prompt:
function Profile({ userId }) {
  if (!userId) return <Login />;

  const [name, setName] = useState('');
  return <input value={name} onChange={e => setName(e.target.value)} />;
}
  • A: renders <Login /> fine, state is discarded
  • B: throws — "Rendered fewer hooks than expected"
  • C: name silently becomes undefined
  • D: React warns in dev, works in prod

questions.text: Is this legal in React 19?
questions.prompt:
import { use } from 'react';

function Message({ promise }) {
  if (!promise) return <Empty />;

  const text = use(promise);
  return <p>{text}</p>;
}
  • A: No — it breaks the rules of hooks
  • B: Yes — use may be called conditionally and inside loops
  • C: Only inside a Server Component
  • D: Yes, but it throws unless wrapped in useMemo
